rationale: Needs both to substantively back different candidates in the same 2026 race; status quo is no qualifying split found. Musk's 2026 money ($276M+) has gone mostly alongside Trump (Paxton in Texas, GOP battlegrounds); his pledged Massie support never became a donation per Massie, and Massie lost in May. With about two weeks left and Musk realigned with the GOP, a qualifying split is unlikely, though an obscure local race or ballot measure could still count.

Republicans need to win any of Maine, Minnesota or North Carolina. North Carolina looks lost (Cooper +8 to +14, Likely D). Minnesota is Flanagan +3 to +4. Maine is Jackson about +2, and Collins has beaten her polls before (2020). In a Democratic-leaning midterm the outcomes are correlated, but a Collins win alone gives roughly 40%, plus a small extra chance from Minnesota.

Needs Lula to win the October 25 runoff by less than 4 points of valid votes. Most mid-October polls (Datafolha, Quaest, MDA) have Flavio ahead by about 2 in valid votes; only Vox Brasil has Lula up 51-49. Flavio also led the first round about 47-45. I put Lula's win chance near 35%, and if he wins, the margin is very likely under 4. A search result showed prediction-market prices, which I ignored.

Kreiss-Tomkins leads every recent poll after ranked-choice rounds (ASR +8, NYT/Siena +4, AARP +10), the RCP average is about +7, and Cook moved the race to Lean D on October 13. The Republican vote is split among three candidates, which helps him unless GOP voters rank each other. Alaska polls have historically underestimated Republicans, and Cook expects a closer finish. A search result showed a market price, which I ignored.

Needs authentic new photo or video of Mojtaba Khamenei by October 31. In about seven months as Supreme Leader, the only official visual was an undated 12-second Mehr clip in August; recent communication is written statements only (October 17), and October reporting says no verified appearance. The base rate of new footage over a two-week window is low.

Lieberman's Yisrael Beiteinu polls at about 9 seats ahead of the October 27 election. The PM contenders are Netanyahu, Eisenkot (Yashar leads some polls) and Bennett. Lieberman becoming PM would need an extraordinary rotation or compromise deal; the historical base rate for a small-party leader is very low.

The resolution hinges on the creator's reading. In April 2026, DEA moved FDA-approved products and state-licensed medical marijuana to Schedule III, but marijuana generally stays in Schedule I. The broader rescheduling hearing ended in July and was reportedly stayed on September 29, with no deadline for a final order, so full rescheduling before November 3 is very unlikely. Whether the partial move counts is roughly a coin flip, leaning NO because the NA clause speaks of removal from Schedule I.

Needs an in-person Russia-Ukraine diplomatic meeting, direct or through mediators, by October 31. Earlier 2026 trilateral rounds in Abu Dhabi and Geneva show these can happen. The US has proposed a technical trilateral by the end of October and Kyiv accepts, but Russia's Ryabkov said on October 7 there are no plans, and Russia is escalating attacks. Little time remains to arrange one.

The Houthis seized Perim/Mayun around September 11. Government forces and outlets claimed full control on October 9-10, but the claims were walked back: AFP and later reports say the island stays in Houthi hands, though the Houthi garrison was reportedly encircled and some fighters sought surrender. Contested control resolves NO, so the government needs to clearly establish control within about 13 days. Its momentum keeps this above the base rate.

Needs a signed final deal with concrete, measurable nuclear limits by November 30. The June MoU expired without extension, talks have stalled over sequencing (Hormuz and blockade versus an enrichment freeze), and Iran's president calls negotiations futile. Some analysts expect a pre-midterm announcement, but the resolution criteria are strict (unconditional measurable obligations, both parties signing). Comprehensive nuclear deals rarely come together this fast.

Polling averages show Peltola ahead by about 1 to 3 points (RCP 48.8-47.4); some polls are ties or have Sullivan narrowly ahead, and one leading pollster's owner is openly anti-Sullivan. Alaska polls have historically underestimated Republicans, and Sullivan is an incumbent in a Trump +13 state, but the national environment favors Democrats. A search result showed a market price, which I ignored.

Incumbent Hobbs leads Biggs in every recent poll (Equis +6, HighGround +17), and averages range from about +5 (DDHQ) to +11 (RCP). The national midterm environment favors Democrats, and incumbent governors usually win reelection. Arizona is swingy and polls can miss, so this stays below 0.85.
